title: Cryptographic Failures
description: Vanaheim demonstrates cryptographic failures through a token generation system using predictable PRNG (Math.random) instead of cryptographically secure random number generation.
theme: Norse realm of fertility gods - where seeds (random seeds) determine harvest (tokens)

vulnerabilities.cwe_name: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

endpoints.description: Verify token and return flag if admin token
Returns recent token history (helps predict next tokens)

vulnerabilities.description: The token generation system uses Math.random() which is not cryptographically secure. By observing multiple generated tokens, an attacker can predict the PRNG state and generate future tokens, including admin tokens.
vulnerabilities.impact: Token prediction, unauthorized access to admin functionality, privilege escalation, session hijacking
exploit_steps: Request multiple guest tokens to observe the pattern
Analyze token generation algorithm (sequential or time-based)
Identify the PRNG seed or pattern
Retrieve flag from successful admin token verification
exploit_indicators: Token patterns showing sequential or predictable values
Tokens generated close in time showing correlation
Math.random() usage in token generation code
Lack of crypto.randomBytes() or similar secure RNG
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use cryptographically secure random number generators: crypto.randomBytes() in Node.js, secrets module in Python, SecureRandom in Java. Never use Math.random(), rand(), or similar functions for security-critical operations. Implement proper token signing (JWT with strong secrets). Use established libraries for token generation.

endpoints.description: JWT tokens signed with predictable secret

vulnerabilities.description: If JWT tokens are used, they may be signed with weak or predictable secrets, allowing token forgery.
vulnerabilities.impact: Token forgery, authentication bypass, privilege escalation
exploit_indicators: Tokens that can be decoded and re-signed
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use strong, randomly generated JWT secrets (minimum 256 bits). Rotate secrets regularly. Store secrets securely (environment variables, key management systems).

flags.retrieval_method: Predict admin token using PRNG analysis, verify to retrieve flag

learning_objectives: Understand difference between PRNG and CSPRNG
Learn about secure random number generation APIs

scanner_test_cases.name: Detect predictable token generation
scanner_test_cases.notes: Generate multiple tokens and analyze for patterns
